title: Compiling Modern C++ and Reading Diagnostics
summary: Build a repeatable C++20 edit-compile-link-run workflow and distinguish compiler, linker, runtime, and logic failures.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Compiling Modern C++ and Reading Diagnostics
Compile and test behavior with observable evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Compile with a modern language mode and strict warnings, for example `c++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic main.cpp -o app`. Source is translated to object code and linked into an executable. Headers normally contain declarations while one or more source files provide definitions. A compiler diagnostic reports an invalid translation unit; a linker error reports a missing or duplicate definition. Read the earliest relevant message, fix one cause, rebuild, and do not run a stale executable after a failed build. Prefer standard facilities over compiler-specific extensions.

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Save the source.
2. Predict diagnostics and output.
3. Compile as C++20 with strict warnings.
4. Fix one cause at a time.
5. Run the executable.
6. Add boundary tests.
